strategies.name: Baseline Sequential All-Reduce Chain
strategies.desc: Executes 8 full all-reduce operations sequentially, each on the complete world_size*2048 tensor, with local bidiagonal coupling/decoupling between reductions. Dispatch count: 8 all-reduces. Represents the straightforward reference with maximal communication cost but minimal code complexity.

strategies.name: Reduce-Scatter + All-Gather Decomposition
strategies.desc: Decomposes each all-reduce into reduce-scatter (producing local shards) followed by all-gather, allowing local bidiagonal operations on smaller S-sized chunks between stages. Dispatch count: 16 reduce-scatters + 16 all-gathers = 32 collectives. Trades more dispatches for smaller per-rank payload and potential for overlapping local compute with communication.

strategies.name: Fused Bidiagonal-Coupling with Batched All-Reduce
strategies.desc: Pre-compute multiple bidiagonal transformations locally, stack them into a batched tensor, then issue a single batched all-reduce covering multiple stages. Dispatch count: 2-4 batched all-reduces. Amortizes dispatch overhead across stages but requires O(stages * world_size * S) temporary memory.

strategies.name: Ring All-Reduce with In-Flight Bidiagonal
strategies.desc: Implements manual ring all-reduce where during each of the world_size-1 send/recv rounds, applies incremental bidiagonal coupling to received chunks before forwarding. Dispatch count: 0 xm all-reduces, replaced by 8 * (world_size-1) point-to-point send/recv pairs. Hides local computation in communication rounds but increases dispatch count significantly.

strategies.name: Hierarchical Two-Level All-Reduce
strategies.desc:
Exploits potential multi-node topology by performing intra-node all-reduce (across cores_per_device * num_devices ranks per node), applying bidiagonal coupling at node granularity, then inter-node all-reduce, followed by broadcast back within nodes. Dispatch count: 8 * (2 intra-node + 1 inter-node + 1 broadcast) = 32 collectives. Benefits from faster intra-node bandwidth but only effective when num_nodes > 1.
